close_reason: Landed commit f14ac4c. Both call sites in MemoryBackend (query_objects ~757, query_changes ~902) now pass the owned String produced by .to_string() directly into State::from rather than going through .as_str() and forcing State's From<&str> impl to allocate a second copy via .to_owned(). Matches the existing Convention A used by three other State::from sites in the same file. Workspace audit (rg State::from with multi-line .to_string().as_str() pattern) found zero sibling occurrences, so cookie-cut scope is empty. No behaviour change; clippy --workspace -D warnings, test --workspace, doc -D warnings all green.
description:
src/memory.rs has two State::from() conventions in the same file:

Convention A (3 sites — lines 415, 480, 926):
    State::from(n.to_string())
    State::from(current_state.to_string())

Convention B (2 sites — lines 505 and 550):
    State::from(
        inner.current_state(O::TYPE_NAME, account_id.as_ref())
            .to_string()
            .as_str(),
    )

State has both From<String> and From<&str> impls (jmap-types/src/id.rs:79-88 via the impl_string_newtype! macro). From<&str> internally calls .to_owned() — so the .as_str() in Convention B is allocating twice (once for to_string(), once for to_owned() inside the impl) for no gain.

Idiomatic Rust uses Convention A everywhere: pass the owned String directly to consume it. The two outliers at lines 505 and 550 should be:

    let query_state = State::from(
        inner.current_state(O::TYPE_NAME, account_id.as_ref()).to_string()
    );

What goes wrong: stylistic inconsistency within one file plus an unnecessary clone on a hot read path (query_objects is called on every Metadata/query). Minor perf, but the readability cost matters — a reader who notices the difference will wonder if the .as_str() is load-bearing.

Cookie-cutter check: the canonical jmap-mail-server's MemoryBackend uses Convention A consistently. metadata-server's Convention B is a divergent regression.

Cookie-cutter propagation: this fix is metadata-server-internal — no canonical change needed. Convention A is already the dominant pattern.
title: MemoryBackend query_objects/query_changes pass State::from(.to_string().as_str()) round-tripping a String through &str
